items.note: OP.0a.P7's PAN HA peer-pairing identity closure (docs/history/phase/OP_0A_PAN_HA_PEER_PAIRING_IDENTITY_CLOSURE.md) found that PAN entity identity (utils.restore_readiness.resolve_entity_id) is hostname-based; hostname is mutable (admin rename), unlike serial, which is already collected on every PAN row in both parsers and already used elsewhere in configuration/panorama_config_collector.py (_collect_direct_compare's identity_mismatch check) as this codebase's own precedent for authoritative device identity. The pairing closure deliberately did not migrate entity_id to serial -- too large a change for a narrow fix, touching every PAN entity_id consumer and existing tests. A deliberate identity-hardening decision belongs before OP.2's identity gate (FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10.1) can depend on PAN pair identity being stable under any real-world hostname change. A hostname-rename-in-place DOES need a data migration for already-persisted records, independent of which option is chosen -- sketched (design only) in the document section 6: recovery vault directories and config-history keys fork at the rename boundary today with zero reconciliation mechanism for PAN (the M8 device_identity_relationships supersession mechanism exists but is CP-only, VENDOR_NAMESPACES=('checkpoint',)). Preliminary lean (not a freeze-ready recommendation): narrow any near-term fix to hardening the existing execution-time serial gate (Option C in the document) rather than migrating resolve_entity_id, but this does not resolve reasons 1 or 2. items.title: CP SSH host-key trust: mandatory strict enforcement for production/container runtime
items.priority: P0 -- production-blocking before production deployment / CLASS 2
items.note: PO decision 2026-09-03 (OP_0B_1_COMMAND_GATE_PACKAGE.md "CP SSH trust -- PO override, development compatibility mode"): the OP.0b S5 CP HA preflight feature (checkpoint.preflight_collector.run_cp_preflight) defaults strict_host_key=False for the current development/pre-production phase, matching every other CP SSH caller's existing compatibility-mode default -- mandatory strict enforcement is deliberately deferred to the future production/container-pod runtime, not implemented now, to avoid investing in workstation-specific Paramiko trust-management machinery ahead of that migration. Strict mode itself remains fully implemented, fail-closed and selectable today via strict_host_key=True; utils.cp_ssh_trust.apply_strict_host_key_policy is unchanged. This item is the production checklist for closing that deferral. Scope: (1) mandatory strict host-key verification for the production runtime -- no compatibility-mode default once containerized; (2) container/pod known_hosts provisioning mechanism (bind-mount or equivalent, matching deploy/secrets/ conventions); (3) independently verified host-key enrollment/provisioning procedure -- no TOFU, no ssh-keyscan-as-trust, out-of-band fingerprint verification required; (4) host-key rotation procedure; (5) mismatch handling (BadHostKeyException stays a distinct, non-retryable, fail-closed rejection); (6) missing-host-key handling (HostKeyNotTrustedError stays a distinct, non-retryable, fail-closed rejection -- see host-key-retry-classification finding below); (7) no automatic promotion of an OBSERVED_UNVERIFIED compatibility-mode fingerprint to trusted status, ever; (8) production startup/preflight should positively prove trusted host-key material exists before the runtime is considered ready, not merely fail closed on first connection attempt; (9) migration away from workstation-specific trust assumptions (a developer's own ~/.ssh/known_hosts) toward a runtime-owned, deployment-provisioned trust store. Host-key-retry-classification finding folded in here rather than a separate item: op0b_s8_host_key_retry_classification (HostKeyNotTrustedError, merged 2026-09-03, PR #47) already made a missing-host-key rejection non-retryable in both CP SSH retry loops; this item tracks keeping that guarantee true as production hardening proceeds, not redoing it. Reconciled with, not duplicating, the narrower cp_ssh_trust_r2_prod_server item (DEPLOY.1 Ubuntu/Docker server R2 validation for the existing CP config-collection path) -- that item's obligation is one line item under this broader checklist. Do not claim strict production hardening is complete until this item closes; the current state is deliberately, explicitly INCOMPLETE by PO decision, not a regression.

NOT treated as resolving this item: not independently re-verified by this session's own code path, root cause of the original discrepancy remains UNKNOWN, and the two observations are not reconciled here. Recorded only as potentially useful future evidence for whoever picks this item up next; do not close from this note alone. UPDATE 2026-09-09 (PAN_SERIAL_REPRESENTATION_IDENTITY_EVIDENCE_CLOSURE_INVESTIGATION, relay NXS-LOCAL-0028): root-cause investigation from source code + already-persisted state only (no live device contact). Full findings in docs/design/PAN_SERIAL_REPRESENTATION_IDENTITY_EVIDENCE_CLOSURE.md. Summary: (1) no raw or tokenized field-level evidence from the S0 run was ever persisted anywhere reachable (project/*.json, docs/history/**, git history, or this profile's runtime root) -- only the narrative MATCH/MISMATCH conclusion survives, so byte-level re-derivation is not possible from what was actually captured; this is itself a real evidence-model gap. (2) A source-code fact not previously flagged: self_identity_consistent/runtime_peer_serial_state compare against row['serial'] (I1, Panorama's show-devices-all discovery cache), computed BEFORE _collect_direct_compare's I1==I2 identity gate runs on the same row -- despite the variable name identity_gated_serial_token and the frozen OP.0b.0 contract's own I3==I2 definition both implying I2. Does not explain this S0 asymmetry on its own (I1==I2 already held for both members per the original note), but is a real naming/contract-vs-implementation gap worth a separate, narrowly-scoped fix. (3) Whitespace/numeric-conversion representation divergence is re-confirmed ruled out by source inspection (all three serial-extraction paths normalize identically). (4) Two independent, pre-existing, real (non-representational) anomalies specific to the same physical member (PAN-3 HA1 config/runtime inconsistency, PAN-12 peer-info completeness) make a genuine member-specific irregularity, or an unconfirmed vendor-semantic difference (D-V3a stays STILL_UNKNOWN in the frozen OP.0b.0 contract -- no official source confirms local-info/serial-num and peer-info/serial-num carry the same value as show-devices-all/show-system-info for every PAN-OS version/HA role), more plausible than a parsing bug. (5) The 2026-09-04 manual show-high-availability-all observation remains unreconciled for concrete reasons (different command, different capture method with no provenance stamp, different time) -- not treated as resolving the MISMATCH finding, which stands as originally recorded. Root cause is NOT conclusively determined. Disposition: RELAY_NOTE / AWAITING_PO appended to relay/NXS-LOCAL-0028-*.json proposing one bounded read-only capture (py main.py --only pan-config --pan-config-targets <serial_A>,<serial_B> --pan-ha-peer-diagnostic against the two already-approved real PAN pair devices) plus an optional additive instrumentation change (persist which pairwise relationship -- I1-vs-I2, I1-vs-I3, I2-vs-I3 -- actually breaks, still booleans only, never raw values) for Product Owner authorization before the next PAN HA identity-evidence movement. items.title: CP preflight: add `cphaprob tablestat` (CCP unique-IP table) as an extra split-brain / control-link evidence source
items.priority: P1 -- valuable evidence, requires a new command-gate row + readiness-contract mapping before implementation
items.target: OP.0b follow-on (post S8 closure); implement only after PO approval of the gate row and the check mapping
items.note: PO request 2026-09-04 (real-environment ClusterXL S8-A, operator-supplied evidence). VENDOR SEMANTIC: `cphaprob tablestat` prints the CCP 'Unique IP's Table' -- for each cluster interface, which members are currently seen exchanging CCP on it (local member rows plus peer member rows, with per-interface IP and MAC). It answers a question the approved battery cannot: `cphaprob -a if` (CP-A4) proves the LOCAL link state of each cluster interface, not that CCP traffic is actually flowing to the peer on it. Operator scenario: one cluster interface physically disconnected while its link reports UP -- `cphaprob -a if` and `cphaprob stat` still look healthy, but the peer's row for that interface disappears from tablestat; that is the precursor to a split-brain election. So tablestat is positive, per-interface, cross-member CCP reachability evidence. WHY NOT ADDED NOW: it is a NEW device command, which is a hard-stop condition of the S8 campaign (new command authority = PO gate, `OP_0B_1_COMMAND_GATE_PACKAGE.md`), and its readiness mapping is a readiness-contract decision, not a parser fix. Nothing in the approved battery changed; `cphaprob -a if` (A4) and `cphaprob -ia list` (A5) are already approved reads and both now parse the real output shapes. WHAT IMPLEMENTATION NEEDS: (1) a gate row modelled on CP-A4 -- Vendor Check Point; Action class CLASS_0_READ; Execution plane device-direct SSH, existing per-member persistent Expert shell; Shell/context Expert direct, physical/VS0; Expected calls per member 1; Concurrency/timeout/retry as CP-A4 (NO_RETRY); Session reuse yes, same session and same INTER_COMMAND_DELAY_SECONDS pacing; Read-only evidence yes (`cphaprob tablestat` is a ClusterXL monitoring command); Evidence category F (link/control health) and/or the split-brain category. (2) SAFE RETAINED FIELDS ONLY -- the raw table carries per-interface IP addresses and MAC addresses: the parser must retain NO address, NO MAC, NO interface name; only bounded counts/booleans: number of cluster interfaces observed, number on which BOTH members are seen, number on which the peer member is absent, and whether the local member is seen on every required interface (cross-referenced only by count against CP-A4's `Required interfaces:`). Structural skeleton diagnostic applies if the shape is unrecognised. (3) READINESS MAPPING (PO decision, not to be invented): candidate checks are `no_split_brain` (peer absent on a required cluster interface = CCP not exchanged = election risk) and `control_sync_link_health` (per-interface CCP reachability, stronger than link state). The classification of 'peer row absent on a required interface' -- FAIL versus INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE -- must be decided against the frozen 'never KNOWN_BAD from absence' law: here the absence is inside the device's own positively-reported table, which is a different thing from a read that produced nothing, but the contract must say so explicitly before the code does. (4) VSX: physical/VS0 context only unless a per-VS semantic is separately established. (5) Tests: parser fail-closed on unknown shape; value-free retained fields (no IP/MAC survives); one call per member in the same shell; battery order and S4 command authority unchanged. Until this item is implemented, the readiness contract keeps its current (weaker) control-link evidence: link state, not CCP exchange. PO APPROVAL 2026-09-09: the Product Owner approved adding the `cphaprob tablestat` gate row (modelled on CP-A4, CLASS_0_READ, one call per member in the existing Expert session, NO_RETRY, value-free retained fields only) and asked for the readiness-contract mapping to be drafted in the same movement for review -- the mapping (FAIL vs INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE for peer-row-absent) is proposed with reasoning against the never-KNOWN_BAD-from-absence law, not silently decided. Dispatched as relay/NXS-LOCAL-0049. 2026-09-09 D-5: HELD until the PO runs cphaprob tablestat on hardware; engineer not resumed.

items.title: tests/test_gov_po_3_ci_privacy_gate_baseline.py's transient scratch fixture can crash a concurrently-running full-repository privacy scan under pytest-xdist
items.target: Test-infrastructure follow-up; discovered incidentally while validating dlp_scanner_prose_collision_in_frozen_records
items.note: Discovered 2026-09-09 (NXS-LOCAL-0042) as one of three failures in an otherwise-successful full one-shot regression: tests/test_nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py::test_ac1_live_bug_regression_against_real_repository_state failed with utils.repository_privacy.RepositoryPrivacyError: cannot safely inspect text candidate: scratch_ac6_synthetic_leak.md. That path is written and then removed by a fixture inside tests/test_gov_po_3_ci_privacy_gate_baseline.py (line ~192), transiently, at the repository root; under `pytest -n auto --dist worksteal` a concurrently-scheduled worker running test_ac1's real filesystem scan of ROOT can observe the file mid-existence and crash on its deliberately-bad encoding before the owning fixture deletes it. Confirmed as a pre-existing, order/parallelism-dependent flake unrelated to this movement's own change: re-running both test files together serially (`pytest tests/test_nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py::test_ac1_live_bug_regression_against_real_repository_state tests/test_gov_po_3_ci_privacy_gate_baseline.py`, no -n) passed 11/11; `git diff --stat` for this movement touches only tests/test_dev_0_5b_auth_consumer_canonical_config.py. Fix direction (not decided/implemented here, out of this movement's DLP-only scope): give the scratch fixture a non-ROOT-colliding location (e.g. a tmp_path-based scratch dir, or a name the privacy scan's own candidate filter structurally excludes) so no cross-test race is possible regardless of xdist scheduling.

items.note:
Objective: let a coding agent (Claude) drive real UI/menu/workflow testing against neXus to reproduce real customer-topology bugs, without the agent ever seeing real device identities, credentials or raw evidence content. FROZEN as of 2026-09-08 for Phase A only: PRIVATE_REPLAY (agent uses an immutable HMAC-pseudonymized dataset derived from a real collection, extending utils/support_bundle.py's existing Tokenizer) and SYNTHETIC_SCENARIO (agent uses fabricated edge cases -- stale peer, timeout, trust mismatch -- absent from the real environment). LIVE_PRIVATE (agent-triggered real collection via a trusted local execution service) is Phase B, deferred design only, not authorized by the freeze -- requires its own separate Product Owner authorization and explicit reconciliation with docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL.md's network-device command gate + utils/action_taxonomy.py before any dispatch.

This session's (2026-09-08) counter-review was accepted in full and folded into the frozen document: (1) offline-first sequencing (Phase A ships before any live-collection design is even authorized, not bundled with the exporter as originally proposed); (2) reuse of the existing AI-initiated-device-command gate rather than a parallel authorization mechanism; (3) isolation testing required from the agent's own actual tool perspective (Read/Bash/env-inspection/process-inspection against a dummy service with synthetic canaries), not just API-malformed-request testing. See the frozen document's own 'Counter-review disposition' section.

Priority raised P0 2026-09-08 per explicit Product Owner direction, scoped to Phase A delivery slices 1-3 only. Phase B stays a separate, later, separately-prioritized item -- this P0 does not cover it.

Slice 1 DELIVERED 2026-09-09 (relay/NXS-LOCAL-0027, engineering session, IMPLEMENTATION movement). Dependency inventory: reused utils/support_bundle.py's Tokenizer (HMAC-SHA256) unchanged as the sole pseudonymization primitive (per this item's own invariant) and its network_token() for network-field typed replacement; genuinely new code is the new replay/ package -- replay/privacy_policy.py (typed, versioned FieldTreatment/FieldPolicy schema realizing the frozen document's 'Privacy compiler' table, plus a fail-closed PrivacyFidelityPolicy.transform() tree-walker: an unclassified field or an unregistered SYNTHESIZE field raises PolicyCoverageError rather than passing the raw value through -- deliberately stricter than support_bundle.py's own _sanitize_dict, which retains unrecognized keys) and replay/isolation.py (ConfinedPackageRoot, the path-confinement primitive every replay provider is built on -- rejects absolute paths, parent traversal and symlink escapes by the same post-resolution containment check utils/runtime_paths.py already uses to keep the runtime and repository roots separate; plus the four explicit replay-provider interfaces the frozen document names for evidence, registry, clock and job execution, with a concrete slice-1 implementation only for the evidence provider -- registry/clock/job stay interfaces, their concrete 'isolated console providers' being slice 3's named work). tests/test_replay_privacy_policy.py and tests/test_replay_isolation.py prove, with synthetic canary secrets (never real credentials/evidence): no canary raw value survives transformation in any position (leaf, nested dict, list); pseudonyms are deterministic for one export key and change with a different key (irreversibility/consistency evidence); and the isolation boundary rejects the frozen document's named agent-tool-perspective adversarial matrix (absolute path, parent traversal, symlinked file, symlinked directory) against a dummy trusted-service directory, with a positive control proving the canary material genuinely exists and a legitimate read genuinely succeeds. Explicitly NOT in slice 1 (left for slice 2/3 per the frozen document's own delivery-slice boundary): the offline typed exporter itself, the package format/validator, vendor-aware raw-configuration synthesis, and any console/UI wiring -- registry/clock/job concrete replay providers stay interfaces only. items.title: UI2 B0/C7 -- backup, artefact and restore engine contract (profile rules per design §6 as amended; store/manifest/validation/retention/key custody from RB contracts; restore execution: plan, preconditions, execute, verify, failure behaviour; per-operation approval; device/version matrix)
items.note: CONTRACT, Sonnet 5 extended (high). RESTORE-IN-RELEASE-1 (D-7) accepted: restore is in Release 1 on declared-supported platforms; a release without it is a "platform pilot / backup collection release". 2026-09-09: dispatched as NXS-LOCAL-0057, Sonnet 5 extended (high). DELIVERED same day -- docs/design/UI2_0_C7_BACKUP_ARTEFACT_RESTORE_ENGINE_CONTRACT.md (DRAFT -- FOR PRODUCT OWNER FREEZE): section 1 states the RAW-RETENTION-vs-backup-artefact-data-class distinction explicitly (raw-retention governs a job step's device transcript only, never the artefact itself); section 2 restates design section 6's profile model field-for-field against C1/C2/C4's real tables (BackupRun/StepResult are C2 jobs/job_step_attempt rows, not new tables; a profile version compiles into a C4 capability_registry row at APPROVED, reusing C4 section 2.4's cp_gaia_backup_local worked example verbatim, not re-derived); section 3 carries forward BACKUP_RECOVERY_CONTRACTS.md sections 2-9 as a Flyway-owned backup_artefact table (the manifest, C1 section 4's encrypted-artefact row), a retention ledger and consistency-group table, with the frozen restore:null reservation re-expressed relationally (a separate restore_run table referencing the artefact, never a column on it); section 4 names the key hierarchy (vault master key wraps a per-artefact DEK, recovery_key_custody.py semantics inherited via C1 section 6.3's env_file pattern) and a concrete rotation procedure (re-wrap the DEK only, never re-encrypt the artefact); section 5 specifies restore plan compilation, a six-check precondition battery, execution via C4's step model, re-collection-based result verification, and a restore-specific OUTCOME_UNKNOWN behaviour (what state the device may be left in across three cases, what a human must verify out-of-band before any retry, and why retry is never automatic); section 6 gives the restore_approval record shape (per-operation, non-reusable, requester != approver) distinct from routine backup's D7-plus-reason shortcut; section 7 fills the device/version matrix template for CP Gaia RB.3b and PAN RB.2, both landing declared_supported=false on their actual inherited evidence (UNPROVEN and FIXTURE_ONLY respectively, neither meeting the REAL_ENV_VALIDATED bar for a class-1 write); section 8 gives 14 acceptance criteria including a restore-failure scenario; section 9 reports two load-bearing open items rather than inventing a fix -- restore's write does not yet fit any utils/action_taxonomy.py class (CLASS_1_RECOVERY_WRITE's own docstring scopes it to "backup creation, exact generated-artifact cleanup", not restore), and C4's closed step-kind set has no device-push/apply step kind (sftp_put is refused unconditionally) -- both named for a taxonomy/C4-successor movement, per this movement's own scope exclusion; action_taxonomy.py is not edited. A third open item flags a documentation inconsistency between UI2_0_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md section 4 ("RB.2 REAL_ENV_VALIDATED") and BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY_ARCHITECTURE.md section 12 ("real-environment validation owed... never mark a network-facing behavior DONE from automated tests alone") -- this document follows the more detailed, conservative source per the fail-closed law. No PO-reserved decision reopened: RESTORE-IN-RELEASE-1, APPROVAL-MODEL and RAW-RETENTION are each implemented as ruled. Not yet FROZEN -- this is the second and final platform-adjacent freeze candidate; freezes independently of C1-C6's own freeze slice per FREEZE-SLICING. 2026-09-09: DELIVERED and PO-accepted -- docs/design/UI2_0_C7_BACKUP_ARTEFACT_RESTORE_ENGINE_CONTRACT.md, PR #170 merged (NXS-LOCAL-0057). Restore is FULLY SPECIFIED but NOT executable: no action_taxonomy.py class fits a restore write, and C4 has no device-directed write step kind (sftp_put unconditionally refused). See ui2_taxonomy_device_write_class_and_step_kind. Not yet FROZEN -- freezes with C1-C6.

items.note: Found by NXS-LOCAL-0057 (C7) SS9.1-9.3, not fixed inside that movement per its own scope boundary and per AGENTS.md's prohibition on inventing a new command class silently. CLASS_1_RECOVERY_WRITE's docstring scopes it to "temporary backup creation, exact generated-artifact cleanup, recovery-specific device operations" -- a restore is none of these; BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY_ARCHITECTURE.md S8 independently classifies restore as "a config-write at the highest blast radius available... sits at the OP.2 bar"; CLASS_2_OPERATIONAL_STATE_CHANGE has no member yet and is scoped to failover, not config restore; CLASS_3_CONFIGURATION_WRITE is prohibited outright at current maturity. Separately, C4 S2.3's closed step-kind set has no device-directed write/push step: sftp_put is "reserved, refused at spec-validation time -- no capability may push bytes to a device at current maturity." Both gaps must close together (C4 S3.3 step 7: a row whose action_class is class 2/3/4 can never be SIGNED_OFF, so a step kind alone does not unblock restore, and a class alone has nothing to carry it). Until this closes, C7's restore engine (docs/design/UI2_0_C7_BACKUP_ARTEFACT_RESTORE_ENGINE_CONTRACT.md S5) is fully specified but not enabled -- same posture as C3's DIRECTORY-POSTURE. NOT auto-dispatched: this is a genuinely new device-write-capable action class, the kind of security boundary the council-trigger process (GOV_PO_ROLE_MIGRATION.md S7) exists for. Recommend a DECIDE episode (or at minimum an explicit PO scoping decision on tier/review depth) before dispatching, rather than routing it through the standard two-at-a-time B0 wave. 2026-09-09: dispatched as NXS-LOCAL-0060 (decision document only, Fable 5.1 medium); PO decides after.
